prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1316; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss came in from the claimant, who reported being rear-ended while stopped at a signal. The claimant is not represented by an attorney and has asked to handle the file directly.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was active at the time of the incident. Nothing in the policy history suggests the damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene. Two statements from people nearby were requested, but no independent witnesses have been identified so far.

Entry 4: Scheduled a physical inspection of the claimant's vehicle. The rear bumper damage and crushed panel are consistent with the impact described in the first notice.

Entry 5: Reviewed the scene photos submitted by the claimant. They confirm several details of the account, though a few older scratches on the rear panel may predate this crash and will need to be separated out in the estimate.

Entry 6: Claimant reported a knee injury and provided initial medical paperwork. It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this collision, and causation remains open pending records.

Entry 7: Claimant called to add a few small details about the seating position and the moment of impact. The core account is unchanged from the first notice. No prior injury to the same knee has been reported or found in the records requested so far.

Entry 8: Treatment records show a usual course of care that tapered off as the claimant improved. Requested the complete chart and prior-provider history to confirm the timeline and any gaps.

Entry 9: File remains open. Next steps are to finish the repair estimate with the older scratches excluded and to complete the causation review of the knee injury before any settlement discussion.
